locator: Song et al. (2019), pp. 3–4; Appendix F.
context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: AIR evaluated 2,458 applicants to 10 Early College High Schools using admissions lotteries in five states.
description: The 2005–06 through 2007–08 applicant cohorts included 1,044 students offered enrollment and 1,414 not offered. The outcome estimates are intent-to-treat effects of an offer, not separate evidence from the report’s complier analysis.

values.value: Lottery-based intent-to-treat evaluation of an offer of enrollment in 10 Early College High Schools versus no offer; Year 10 is six years after expected high-school graduation.

context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: An Early College offer increased any college enrollment by Year 10 by 7.2 percentage points (84.2% versus 77.0%; p < .001).
description: This is the intent-to-treat effect of being offered enrollment in the 10-school lottery study. It measures any postsecondary enrollment by Year 10, not degree completion or an effect for every Early College model.

values.value: Percentage-point intent-to-treat difference in any college enrollment by Year 10, offer minus no offer.

context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: An Early College offer increased any postsecondary degree by Year 10 by 11.9 percentage points (45.4% versus 33.5%; p < .001).
description: This intent-to-treat estimate covers any postsecondary degree in the lottery-study sample. It does not isolate a particular Early College component or establish a lifetime earnings effect.

values.value: Percentage-point intent-to-treat difference in earning any postsecondary degree by Year 10, offer minus no offer.

context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: An Early College offer increased associate-degree or certificate attainment by Year 10 by 18.2 percentage points (29.3% versus 11.1%; p < .001).
description: This is the intent-to-treat effect for associate degrees or certificates in the lottery-study sample. It should not be combined with the bachelor’s estimate as independent study evidence.

values.value: Percentage-point intent-to-treat difference in associate-degree or certificate attainment by Year 10, offer minus no offer.

context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: An Early College offer increased bachelor’s-degree attainment by Year 10 by 5.2 percentage points (30.1% versus 24.9%; p = .037).
description: This is the intent-to-treat bachelor’s-degree result from the same lottery evaluation and horizon as the other attainment records. It is not a separate replication.

values.value: Percentage-point intent-to-treat difference in bachelor’s-degree attainment by Year 10, offer minus no offer.

context: Early College long-term follow-up; extracted from the reviewed batch.
name: An Early College offer showed a 0.8-point difference in four-year-college enrollment by Year 10 (57.6% versus 56.7%; p = .744).
description: The report’s intent-to-treat estimate is not statistically distinguishable from zero for this outcome. It does not negate the study’s other enrollment and degree findings.

values.value: Percentage-point intent-to-treat difference in enrollment at a four-year college by Year 10, offer minus no offer.
